content: Leisure without study is death—a tomb for the living man.
author: Seneca
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

Seneca understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
